You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer runtime-linux):
- file: runtime/linux/loader.c:24
- category: duplication
- title: SimControl device base 0xe0080000 re-declared as a third private magic constant
- detail: loader.c line 24 defines `#define HTIF_MMIO_BASE 0xe0080000UL`; the same address already exists as `SIM_EXIT_ADDR 0xe0080000UL` in runtime/vplat_syscalls.c line 19 (and as a literal in runtime/crt0.S line 101). runtime/htif_client.h is the declared owner of the SimControl device layout (it documents 'SimControl exit @0xe0080000' in prose and defines WIN_DATA_VA 0xe0080840; htif_client.c defines the doorbell 0xe0080028 and slots 0xe0080800). loader.c's own comment (lines 21-23) even points at htif_client.h as the source of this layout, then re-declares the base privately anyway. Hoisting one `SIM_CONTROL_BASE` (and the 0x1000 window size) into htif_client.h and deriving SIM_EXIT_ADDR / HTIF_MMIO_BASE from it gives the C sites one source of truth (crt0.S is assembly and can stay as-is).
- claimed safety: All three sites hold the identical value today; replacing two private defines with one shared define whose value is unchanged produces identical object code.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

1	#ifndef ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H
2	#define ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H
3	
4	/* HTIF syscall-window client: the uncached SimControl mailbox protocol
5	 * shared by every andesim runtime payload (vplat today; vlinux next). The
6	 * window lives in DEVICE space (PMA-uncached on every engine), so the
7	 * exchange is coherent by construction on any cache hierarchy, including a
8	 * private write-back L2 (ax66 PL2C) that a cacheable-RAM mailbox cannot
9	 * survive: the guest would read its own stale copy of the host's result,
10	 * and no guest-side CCTL sequence can fix that (the VA-scoped forms trap
11	 * on RVH cores, the ALL forms drop unrelated dirty lines).
12	 *
13	 *   stdio (fd 0-2)  ATCUART100 UART2: THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034.
14	 *   file io (fd>2)  the SimControl syscall WINDOW @0xe0080800: eight u64
15	 *                   arg/result slots + a data area for payloads, doorbell
16	 *                   @0xe0080028. Served host-side (vsim: sim_control.hpp
17	 *                   dispatch_window; QEMU: andes_ae350.c's mirror).
18	 *
19	 * No semihosting, no ecall, and no "which engine am I on" probe -- hybrid
20	 * migrates the running process between engines, so any boot-time detection
21	 * would go stale at the handoff. Every call must be engine-blind.
22	 */
23	
24	#include <stddef.h>
25	#include <stdint.h>
26	#include <sys/types.h>
27	
28	/* HTIF syscall numbers -- must match the table in the vsim repo's
29	 * src/platform/sim_control.hpp (and the QEMU mirror device). */
30	#define VH_SYS_GETTIMEOFDAY 5
31	#define VH_SYS_OPEN         6
32	#define VH_SYS_WRITE        7
33	#define VH_SYS_GETCWD       8
34	#define VH_SYS_LSEEK        9
35	#define VH_SYS_READ         10
36	#define VH_SYS_FLEN         11
37	#define VH_SYS_CLOSE        12
38	#define VH_SYS_ACCESS       13
39	#define VH_SYS_FACCESSAT    14
40	#define VH_SYS_FSTAT        15
41	#define VH_SYS_FSTATAT      16
42	#define VH_SYS_LINK         17
43	#define VH_SYS_LSTAT        18
44	#define VH_SYS_STAT         19
45	#define VH_SYS_OPENAT       20
46	#define VH_SYS_RENAME       21
47	#define VH_SYS_UNLINK       22
48	
49	/* Window layout -- must match the hosts (vsim src/platform/sim_control.hpp
50	 * SYSCALL_WINDOW_*; QEMU hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c ANDESIM_SYSCALL_*). All
51	 * guest accesses are u64 loads/stores (the access width every engine
52	 * already proves out on the legacy 0x10 doorbell). */
53	#define WIN_DATA_VA 0xe0080840UL
54	#define WIN_DATA_SIZE (0x800u - 0x40u) /* 1984 bytes, 8-aligned */
55	
56	/* Console output; blocks until UART2's transmit-holding register drains. */
57	void htif_uart_putc(char c);
58	
59	/* One window syscall: stage the slots, ring the doorbell, read the result.
60	 * The doorbell write is an uncached device store, so the host has served
61	 * the call before the store retires; the fence orders the result load. */
62	intptr_t htif_syscall(uint64_t n, uint64_t a0, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2,
63	                       uint64_t a3);
64	
65	/* Raw copies into/out of the window data area (u64 accesses only). `woff`
66	 * is a byte offset into the data area and must be 8-aligned. */
67	void htif_win_store(size_t woff, const void* src, size_t len);
68	void htif_win_load(void* dst, size_t woff, size_t len);
69	
70	/* Stage a string at data-area offset `woff`; returns the byte offset just
71	 * past its NUL, rounded up to 8, or (size_t)-1 if it does not fit. */
72	size_t htif_win_store_str(size_t woff, const char* s);
73	
74	/* Marshaling helpers for the recurring one/two-string-argument shapes. */
75	intptr_t htif_call_str(uint64_t n, const char* s, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2);
76	intptr_t htif_call_str2(uint64_t n, const char* s0, const char* s1);
77	
78	/* fd>2 write/read, chunked through the window data area (WIN_DATA_SIZE
79	 * bytes per round trip); stops early on a short transfer, same contract as
80	 * a POSIX write()/read(). Callers own the fd<=2 (console) special case. */
81	ssize_t htif_write(int fd, const void* ptr, size_t len);
82	ssize_t htif_read(int fd, void* buf, size_t len);
83	
84	/* Positional read: seeks to `offset`, reads `len` bytes via htif_read,
85	 * then restores the fd's original position -- there is no pread window
86	 * op, only lseek+read, so this is the only way to honor pread(2)'s "does
87	 * not disturb the fd's current offset" contract on top of them. Shared by
88	 * every positional-read caller (syscall pread64, file-backed mmap) so the
89	 * save/restore sequence exists in exactly one place. */
90	ssize_t htif_pread(int fd, void* buf, size_t len, long offset);
91	
92	#endif /* ANDESIM_HTIF_CLIENT_H */
93
